title: Rollout Simulation Playground and Safety Templates
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design an interactive 'Rollout Simulation Playground' inside the Redwood Console to let engineers and product owners rehearse canary, A/B, and traffic-split rollouts before applying them to production. The playground will surface safety templates (e.g., strict, conservative, exploratory), allow replaying a sample of historical traffic or synthetic scenarios, and visualize simulated outcomes across key signals (latency, error rate, cost per token, quality regression score). The goal is to reduce misconfigurations, build confidence for rollouts, and shorten the feedback loop for safety policy selection.
background: Current console flows let users create canary/A-B experiments and define traffic percentages, but teams request a safer way to preview the operational impact of those choices without waiting for real traffic. PM research (customer interviews) indicates fear of regressions and unclear rollback impact. Engineering warns about expensive full-fidelity simulations. This design tries to balance fidelity, clarity, and speed.
goals: Provide an easy-to-understand simulation UI for canary/A-B/traffic-splits
Offer curated safety templates (strict, default, aggressive) with one-click apply
Visualize projected metrics and confidence intervals for each variant/cohort
Allow 'what-if' scenario runs including sudden traffic spikes and rollback exercises
Export simulator configuration to rollout YAML to apply or schedule in Console
non_goals: Full production-grade replay of millions of requests (engineering will provide replay sampler)
Replacing the existing rollout creation flow immediately; this is an adjunct rehearsal tool
Automated automatic rollback execution (simulator recommends but does not enact)
user_personas: Platform engineer scheduling a canary to validate latency for a new quantized model
Product manager running A/B tests to evaluate quality vs cost tradeoffs
SRE assessing rollback impact and drafting runbooks
flows: Start new simulation -> Choose source (synthetic traffic / small sampled trace / production replay stub)
Choose rollout strategy (Canary / A-B / Traffic Split) and define cohorts/weights
Select safety template or create custom SLOs and abort conditions
Run simulation: time-slider shows progression, timeline charts display metrics per cohort
Trigger simulated rollback or fast-forward to see recovery and cost delta
Export configuration or apply to a non-production environment, save simulation to library
acceptance_criteria: Design includes a clear selection UI for 'source' that distinguishes synthetic vs sampled replay
At least three safety templates are defined with editable thresholds and clear descriptions
Visualization shows at-a-glance projected delta for latency, error rate, and token cost per minute
Users can run a 5-minute simulated rollout in under 15s of perceived time using time-scaling
Simulator output can be exported as a rollout YAML and imported into the existing rollout creation flow

design_decisions: Simulation fidelity: use statistical sampling + deterministic noise model rather than full replay to keep costs low
Safety templates are opinionated presets with suggested abort gates, editable by users to match org risk tolerance
Simulator will be feature-flagged behind 'simulator-beta' and accessible in non-prod accounts by default
Simulator recommendations will be advisory only; any 'apply' action routes user to the standard rollout flow to ensure audit trail
tradeoffs: Fidelity vs cost: Lower-fidelity simulations will be faster/cheaper but may miss edge-case regressions
Complexity vs clarity: Offering many knobs increases power but risks confusing non-expert users; templates mitigate this
Automation vs safety: Avoid auto-execution from the simulator to keep human-in-the-loop and preserve access controls
